answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce tokens before voting on reputation or claiming rewards. A nebula of fake agents must each tie up capital, while influence depends on stake and lock duration rather than account count. A coordinated pulse of registrations then buys little power unless the attacker commits more funds, which can be forfeited for misconduct. At a summit of validators, the rules can be reviewed, but the attacker still pays the cost of capital at risk.
